          Title: Ecclesiae Graecae Monumenta (Cotelier), including the Vita Sabae and
                  Vita Euthymii of Cyril of Scythopolis
     Creator(s): Cyril of Scythopolis (c. 525-559 CE)
                 Cotelier (Jean-Baptiste Cotelier) (Editor, Greek text with Latin
                  translation)
    Print Basis: Paris, 1681 (Ecclesiae Graecae Monumenta)
         Rights: Public Domain
       Language: grc+lat
   Rights Basis: Published 1681; long out of US copyright. Confirmed directly from the
                  Internet Archive/Google Books scan (identifier bub_gb_1Z5eE88JWfIC),
                  fetched and read in full this session.
Source Collection: Internet Archive (archive.org), identifier bub_gb_1Z5eE88JWfIC
   Content note: Same source-gap report as above, citing ch. 83-90 of the Vita Sabae
                  ("the New Laura is emptied") - the report itself notes Schwartz's
                  standard 1939 critical edition is still in copyright, making this 1681
                  Cotelier edition the only public-domain option. CAUTION, disclosed
                  rather than resolved: this is a 17th-century typeface scan with heavy
                  OCR corruption (long-s misread throughout, Greek/Latin parallel
                  columns frequently interleaved wrong by the OCR). Both the Vita
                  Euthymii (confirmed, "EUTHYMII VITA" header present) and the Vita
                  Sabae itself (confirmed via "De vita Sabae" and "in Vita S. Sabae"
                  references) are genuinely present in this volume, but the specific ch.
                  83-90 New Laura passage was NOT pinpointed - the volume's own back-of-
                  book index uses page numbers that do not map cleanly to this raw OCR
                  text's line numbers. Any future quote drawn from this file needs
                  unusually careful individual eye-verification given the OCR quality;
                  this is a materially worse source than this corpus's typical vendored
                  texts.
     ______________________________________________________________________

NOTE ON THIS TRANSCRIPTION: the source is a raw OCR (djvu) text layer from
a scanned physical volume, not a clean digital edition. Runs of 2+ spaces
between words (a systematic OCR-layout artifact of the scan, not a feature
of the printed text) have been collapsed to single spaces throughout; no
word, spelling, or punctuation has been altered. OCR misreads may remain
uncorrected elsewhere in the file; any passage this build quotes verbatim
has been checked by eye against this file directly, not assumed correct
from the OCR alone.
